tagline: Three miles of turnpike in the water company's woods.
intro: From the Fairfield line Route 58, the Black Rock Turnpike, runs three miles north through Easton beside the Hemlock Reservoir, one of two lakes along this road that give the Bridgeport area much of its drinking water.

Easton was slow to settle because of the rough hills along the Aspetuck River, and it did not part from Weston until 1845. Today the water company owns half the property in town. Helen Keller spent her last years here.

moments.title: Hemlock Reservoir
moments.text: Behind a dam finished in 1914, the reservoir holds largemouth bass, chain pickerel and rainbow trout, and fishing is prohibited.

moments.title: Redding Road
moments.text: On April 25, 1777, General William Tryon's British troops marched up the old Redding Road, which ran alongside this one, on their way to raid Danbury.
